blocks.raw:
<Tip>
**Memory Aid:** End-bearing piles say "I stand on a rock"; friction piles say "I hug the soil." Batter piles lean to fight sideways forces. Sheet piles lock arm-in-arm to hold back the earth wall. Diameter 600 mm is the magic threshold: below is a pile, at or above is a caisson.
</Tip>

blocks.raw: <WikiMistakeList mistakes={["Confusing batter piles with bored piles; batter refers to inclination (1:6–1:12), not installation method.","Assuming all drilled piles are cast in place with reduced skin friction; proper borehole preparation and tremie placement preserve friction capacity.","Stating that sheet piles transfer load to the foundation; they are a retaining system, not a load-bearing element.","Using pile and caisson interchangeably without respect to the ≥ 600 mm diameter threshold that governs excavation, integrity testing, and behavior.","Omitting pile caps in load distribution sketches; caps are mandatory to distribute superstructure load across multiple piles."]} />
